H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a flat four-state FSM: wait, wander, grasp, give; no parent/child or composite state structure is specified.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on simple conditions/events such as command sent and object/user reached; no arithmetic, thresholds, or multi-variable boolean guards are given for the FSM.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include locating the glass/user with landmarks, reaching by shortest path, bending over, taking the glass, and offering it to the user.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No emergency stop, fault state, rollback, abort, or recovery path is described for the robot FSM.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and their main actions are co-located in the same robot-system description around Figure 1, with later text only restating the autonomous mode.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as autonomous mode, landmarks, and shortest path do not imply unstated state-transition rules that must be decoded from external domain knowledge.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The action prose is directly attached to the state names: in grasp state the robot bends and takes the glass; in give state it bends and offers it.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: No guard combines multiple variables, arithmetic, or boolean composition.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: There is no composite state, hence no parent-level entry/during/exit behavior.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or global recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The FSM has no arithmetic or boolean guard set requiring SMT-style consistency checking.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting forced transition or parent-level during monitor is specified.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete robot behaviors rather than effector-agnostic logging, publishing, alerting, or notification actions.

key_nl_quotes: The robot starts in the wait state. When a command is sent, the robot enter in wander mode to acquire the position of the glass or the user with landmarks.

After the object/user has been reached, he acts accordingly to grasp or give state. In grasp state, the robot will bend over and take the glass, in give state it will bend over and offers the glass to the user.
one_line_pitch: This is a readable flat assistive-robot FSM whose stress-test value is limited mainly to recovering a narrative action chain rather than hierarchy, rich guards, or recovery behavior.
rationale: The paper provides a genuine FSM for autonomous BCI-controlled robot behavior, but it is structurally simple: four flat states with direct command and target-reached transitions. It has meaningful robot actions, yet lacks hierarchy, arithmetic or multi-variable guards, and any fault-recovery pattern. Because H+G+A+F totals only 3, it falls below the benchmark stress-test threshold.
